#1689. Barcelona transfer news: Catalan giants could receive £10m windfall from PSG transfer

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 08:45

Paris Saint-Germain could indirectly do Barcelona a favour in the January transfer window. In search of a potential attacking reinforcement after the long-term injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, the capital club have drawn up an initial shortlist.

According to AS, Antonio Nusa is among the capital club's preferred targets, alongside Abde Ezzalzouli, Gianluca Prestianni, Ibrahim Maza, Luis Diaz and Estevao. These players will be difficult to sign in the January transfer window. Paris have already experienced that, having been rebuffed over Estevao, while Prestianni wants to finish the season at Benfica.

In that sense, Abde Ezzalzouli could be an interesting option. 3Cat confirms that the Morocco international is among the targets being studied by PSG to strengthen their attack in January. Aged 24, Abde is enjoying a good start to the season, with four goals and one assist in 13 games for the Andalusian club.

His profile has reportedly caught the attention of the Parisian hierarchy, especially as the player now shares the same agent as Achraf Hakimi.

This could ease discussions. The rumour is also being followed closely in Barcelona, as a potential transfer of the Real Betis winger would allow Barcelona to recoup a significant sum.

The Catalan outlet recalls that in September 2023, Barcelona sold Abde to Real Betis for £6.4m (€7.5m). In that deal, they kept a share of the Moroccan's economic rights. Initially set at 50%, it was later reduced to 20% in February 2025 as part of the agreement concerning Vitor Roque.

A £51m (€60m) transfer, the amount of Abde's release clause, would therefore bring Barcelona £10m. PSG would have the opportunity to sign a promising 24-year-old winger for a reasonable amount, while doing their Spanish rivals a serious financial favour by triggering the clause.

This sum could give the Barcelona hierarchy more room for manoeuvre to strengthen Hansi Flick's squad this winter. The German boss is notably looking to sign a centre-back.

It should be noted that, at this stage, no agreement or advanced negotiation has been announced for Abde's arrival at PSG. It remains to be seen whether Paris will actually take action.

#1688. Manchester United dealt blow as Mauricio Pochettino drops hint in confirmed Champions League squad

Manchester United are set to welcome Luke Shaw and Karl Darlow back into the fold for tomorrow night’s Champions League trip to Sporting, but they will be without Matheus Cunha, who was left out of the travelling cohort.

The Brazilian was withdrawn at half time in the 4-0 drubbing from Liverpool over the weekend, replaced by Joshua Zirkzee as the Red Devils trailed 2-0 and were down to ten men after Leny Yoro’s now-overturned red card.

The former Wolves forward is sidelined due to a suspension he picked up from his red card against Roma last time out in Europe.

The return of Shaw, meanwhile, will be appreciated by new boss Mauricio Pochettino, who has the enviable task of shaping a defence that has conceded 34 goals in 18 matches so far this season.

The left-back has missed United’s last eight fixtures with a muscular issue, but the former Southampton defender was pictured in training ahead of Wednesday night’s game.

The 31-year-old is yet to feature in the Champions League this season, rested for the 4-0 win in the opener over Sabah, before injury ruled him out of the next three fixtures.

Backup goalkeeper Darlow has made just one appearance for the Red Devils since joining from rivals Leeds in the summer.

The Welshman was called up for international duty a fortnight ago, playing the first game of the break against Norway before being rested for the second due to a knock.

Darlow was not fit enough to be named on the bench for Sunday’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool at Anfield, but the 36-year-old was also spotted in training ahead of the Sporting game.

#1687. How Arsenal will change tactics to suit Kepa in goalkeeper’s last chance to impress

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Any and all updates on David Raya were welcome if you were an Arsenal fan.

There were the attempts to lip read what head physio Simon Murphy said as he walked off the St James’ Park pitch with Raya.

Then the sighting of Raya the following day in Oxford Circus with his arm in a sling. And the report that he had been able to drive himself home after the club returned to London from Newcastle.

The sense of panic was understandable. Raya is Arsenal’s most irreplaceable player, pivotal to the team not just because of his shot-stopping, but the way he commands his area and how central he is to the build-up in possession as well.

It was good news, then, that he has avoided a serious injury. Raya has not yet been ruled out of facing Manchester City this weekend.

Even with the outlook more positive than it might have been, Arsenal must still find a way to cope without the Spaniard for at least tonight’s match against Borussia Dortmund.

This will be a big night for Kepa Arrizabalaga. He started against Kairat Almaty last season, but that dead rubber aside has not played in the Champions League since making four appearances for Real Madrid in the competition in 2023.

This is a chance to prove he still belongs at this level. Kepa will surely still have an eye on becoming a first-choice goalkeeper again at a top club elsewhere in the seasons ahead. However, that kind of evidence has been in short supply since he arrived at Arsenal.

Mikel Arteta put his faith in Kepa last season in the Carabao Cup final and it was not repaid. Kepa was booked for hauling down Jeremy Doku after misjudging a bouncing ball, before gifting City the lead when spilling a cross.

His distribution, too, was poor. Throughout the match, Arsenal’s build-up was almost entirely nullified by City and that started with the goalkeeper.

A key facet of Arsenal’s build-up is Raya’s ability to not just go short, but to ping flat, long passes up the pitch to play over the press when required.

It is easy to forget just how highly rated Kepa once was, he remains the most expensive goalkeeper signing of all time

Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund: Champions League - LIVE

Can Nwaneri play against Arsenal in Champions League tonight?

Why isn’t Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund on TNT Sports tonight?

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

“David Raya can play six, I swear,” Noni Madueke said in a recent interview.

Kepa cannot play those same passes with the same trajectory or accuracy. Nor is he as convincing in inspiring the same confidence when going short under pressure.

Asked on Monday whether Arsenal would have to change how they play without Raya, Arteta said: “We adapt to players’ qualities, and they all have different ones.

“There are certain things that, in our game or in the way that we understand the game and we want to play the game, everybody has to be 100% committed to, but then we make adjustments in relation to the qualities of the players.”

One of those adjustments will have to be how Arsenal build up. Illan Meslier would be more comfortable in that respect, with the ball at his feet, but he is liable to make big mistakes and can be exposed when the ball is crossed on top of him.

There has never been any real consideration from Arteta or his coaching staff that it would be Meslier getting the nod over Kepa to stand in for Raya.

When he signed in the summer, Meslier was aware of the pecking order. He arrived primarily to allow Tommy Setford to go out on loan, rather than to replace Kepa as No2.

Meslier started in the Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood, even with Kepa fit and in the squad. However, that was due to a desire to reward Meslier for his consistency in training and impact on the squad, not a rejigging of the pecking order.

It is easy to forget just how highly rated Kepa once was. He remains the most expensive goalkeeper signing of all time, joining Chelsea for £72million in 2018.

That price tag has followed him around ever since. So too Carabao Cup finals, both last season’s horror show and the 2019 edition when he refused to be substituted.

The temptation is to say a quiet night, one in which he is not noticed against Dortmund, would be ideal for Kepa, but Raya does not have many of those.

Even when he is not required to pull off saves, he is still making line-breaking passes or pushing up close to the halfway line to snuff out attacks.

Kepa failed on all those counts in the Carabao Cup final last season. Another poor performance this time and it is hard to see how he can retain Arteta’s trust.

In his biggest test since that Wembley occasion, Arsenal need Kepa to minimise the disruption of Raya’s absence.

#1686. Bayern must find solutions in Olise and Kane’s absence, says Kompany

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Vincent Kompany quipped Bayern Munich are missing "130 goals from last season" ahead of their Champions League trip to Lille, with Harry Kane and Michael Olise unavailable.

Bayern arrive at Stade Pierre-Mauroy just days after it was announced that Ballon d'Or winner Kane is set to miss the next few months with an ankle ligament injury sustained against Koln.

Kane has either scored or assisted in each of his last 11 games in the Champions League, which is currently the joint-longest run, along with Cristiano Ronaldo (between 2017 and 2018) and Ruud van Nistelrooy (between 2002 and 2003).

The England captain has 10 goals and 11 assists in all competitions this season, with Kompany also without Olise, who has failed to recover from an issue with his foot.

Olise has 18 goal involvements (12 goals, six assists) across all competitions this season, the sixth-highest tally across Europe's top five leagues in 2026-27.

Kane and Olise join an extensive list of injuries for Kompany to contend with. Serge Gnabry, Ismael Saibari, Alphonso Davies and Manuel Neuer are also sidelined.

Bayern have scored in each of their last 25 Champions League matches, dating back to January 2025, but he said they must find different ways to attack against Lille.

"It's about always being realistic and finding solutions – then getting the results," Kompany told reporters.

"130 goals from last season aren't there, but we have guys who can run and fight. Then we have our fans too. We're going into the match with hunger and desire.

"We want to show that we're Bayern Munich on the pitch."

Next up: back under the Champions League lights. https://t.co/xYqATNhcpq

— FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) November 22, 2026

Kompany did, however, have some good news on the injury front, with Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz both expected to play at least some part in Wednesday's clash.

The only previous meetings between Lille and Bayern came in the group stage of the 2012-13 Champions League, with the Germans winning home (6-1) and away (1-0).

Since the start of last season, Bayern's only two defeats in 18 Champions League matches (W13 D3) have been against the 2026 finalists Paris Saint-Germain (April this year) and Arsenal (November 2025).

And they come up against a Lille side who are on a six-game winless run in Europe (D1 L5). Only once have they had a longer run without a victory in major European competition (13 games between December 2012 and December 2019).

"Until last week, they were second in France. They always have a lot of talent; they're well known for their academy," Kompany said of Lille.

"They have a lot of pace on the counter; they defend aggressively from the front. They've got a few guys with international experience as well.

"They'll want to put on a show at home. I expect high pressure and a good game for the spectators."

#1685. Jashari delighted after ‘beautiful’ Frosinone win and first Milan goal: “I promised the fans”

Ardon Jashari claims he promised the AC Milan fans he would score, so he was happy to deliver on his promise.

Milan put on a counter-attacking clinic at San Siro on Sunday night against Frosinone, winning 5-1. An own-goal from Gabriele Calvani kicked things off, with Goncalo Ramos, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic also netting.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There was a special moment for Jashari just after coming on at half-time as he scored the third goal of the night and his first for the club. It came in transition, with the Swiss midfielder running in behind and thumping a powerful shot in off the near post, leaving the goalkeeper stunned.

Jashari spoke to SportMediaset after the final whistle at San Siro to reflect on what was a great night both for the team and for him on a personal note, with his words via MilanPress.

“Finally, I’m very happy with my first goal for Milan. It was a great feeling, and I’m happy for our team. We played a very intense, beautiful game against a tough and united team, both on and off the ball. We won, and we have to continue like this on Thursday, and for the rest of the season.”

“I hope so. I’m happy with today and I’ll try to continue like this for the team and the fans. It’s very important to have won.”

⚽️ GOAL ARDON JASHARI! His first for #ACMilan! 👏 https://t.co/fdfHgOJtfJ

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026

What can you tell us about your position today?

“I played next to Luka today. Normally, strikers score goals, but today it was my turn. When I score, I score beautiful goals (smiles). It seemed like the goal against Venezia, but today it was even better because it was mine. The celebration was the same. I promised the fans I would score, and that’s what happened.”

“In my opinion, it’s very important to continue like this. The season is too long until May. Now it’s November. We’ve had a good season so far, but there are five months to go until May. We need these results against all our opponents. Today it was Frosinone, there’s still a lot to do.

“When you play for Milan, you have to win games and trophies, but it’s November. Everyone knows what it means to wear the Milan shirt, it’s important to continue like this. When you win, you’re good, when you lose, you’re not. It doesn’t matter who scores.”

#1684. Arsenal XI vs Borussia Dortmund: Starting lineup, confirmed team news and injury latest for Champions League

Arsenal dropped points from a winning position for the second time in as many games following a 1-1 Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium.Mikel Arteta’s men led at the interval after Viktor Gyokeres scored his first goal on home soil in 206 days with a wonderful 25-yard opener inside 10 minutes.

But just as they did in the Premier League at Newcastle on Saturday, Arsenal were unable to see out the victory, with Maximilian Beier netting for the visitors after half-time. Jobe Bellingham had a goal ruled out for offside, while Gyokeres could perhaps count himself fortunate not to give away a penalty when a Dortmund corner struck him on the arm.

Gyokeres then wasted a golden opportunity to restore Arsenal’s advantage when he headed wide unmarked from six yards, while the ball cannoned off Serhou Guirassy to twice strike the Dortmund post in the closing stages. Declan Rice hit the woodwork again for Arsenal with five minutes left.

Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund latest updates

Here was Arsenal’s very own Groundhog Day. Again.

Mikel Arteta would have feared what was coming as the misses piled up and his team found increasingly remarkable ways to not score.

It was rinse and repeat from an Arsenal perspective. Completely dominate the opening 45 minutes with some sublime football. Take the lead but then fail to kick on. Drop the intensity in the second half and regret those missed opportunities.

How did Matt Verri rate the Arsenal players?

There we have it. Arsenal are held, the spoils are shared.

Thanks for joining us, be sure to come back very soon for even more live action.

80 mins: Free kick, Arsenal. Handball by Sabitzer. Another chance for the hosts to hoist one into the box towards their big lads.

#1683. Kevin De Bruyne responds to Man City "disgrace" claims after Premier League guilty verdict

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 09:01, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 10:51

Kevin De Bruyne has made his feelings for Manchester City crystal clear as he has spoken out for the first time since the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations.

At the end of September, an independent commission found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the investigation.

The Citizens are accused of using "sham" contracts with a number of commercial partners to disguise secret funding of more than £830m and artificially inflate revenues between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

Man City continue to plead their innocence and lodged an appeal last month, stating that “a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.”

A plethora of possible sanctions have been mooted should Man City’s guilty verdict be upheld, including heavy fines, transfer bans, stripping titles, points deductions leading to relegation and expulsion from the Premier League.

De Bruyne spent 10 glorious years at the Etihad Stadium before leaving in the summer of 2025 and will go down as one of Man City’s greatest-ever players after playing a crucial role in the club winning 19 trophies during his time at the club.

The Belgian playmaker won six Premier League titles, five EFL Cups and three FA Cups, while he also won the Champions League during a historic treble-winning season in 2022-23.

The two-time Premier League Player of the Season scored 108 goals and provided 177 assists in 422 appearances for Man City across all competitions, with 119 of those assists recorded in the Premier League to rank him second on the all-time list behind Ryan Giggs (162).

De Bruyne has made a welcome retuned to Manchester as his current club Napoli prepare to face City in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

While De Bruyne has acknowledged that some people may have different opinions over Man City’s guilty verdict, the legendary midfielder himself has insisted that his feelings towards the club will “never change”.

"My feeling's never been different,” he told reporters at a press conference. “Honestly, the way that I feel is just the way that I've been treated by this club, what I've done with this club for me personally, and how we've worked together as a group. Of course, it's a lot of things that's been going on but I cannot change anything about that.

"I'm proud of what I've done as a football player, and honestly... This is my club! I love the owners, I've talked about a lot of stuff outside of football, I've even spoken to Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] how to buy a club and everything, so there's a lot of things that goes around after this.

"I've nothing but affection for this club and that will never change! Even now, the people who treated me for 10 years exceptionally, my family and everything, that's for me the most important and for me, that is it to be honest."

Intense criticism has been aimed at Man City since the guilty verdict, but De Bruyne cannot "change anything" about people calling his former club a "disgrace" and still believes that everything he personally achieved with the club was won fairly.

“It [the verdict] still doesn’t change, my football has not changed,” De Bruyne said. “In life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit.

“I played in between the white lines, I competed with other players and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players. That’s the thing I value most.

“In my career, the most important thing is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things.

“I’ve given my all and that’s not going to change in my mind. I don’t think a lot of ­people will change in their mind how they view me as a player or how we played. Other people may be disgraced a bit, but I can’t change anything about that.”

Tuesday’s contest will mark De Bruyne’s second appearance back at the Etihad since departing Man City, and the 35-year-old will be hoping for a much smoother evening this time around.

On his previous visit last year, a first-half red card forced ex-Napoli boss Antonio Conte to reshuffle his side, with De Bruyne the unfortunate player to be sacrificed early in a 2-0 defeat.

#1681. Emery picked ‘best players to be here with Villa’ amid Garnacho snub

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Unai Emery claimed Alejandro Garnacho was excluded from Aston Villa's Champions League squad against Galatasaray due to picking the "best players to be here with us".

Villa were below par against Galatasaray, falling to a 1-0 defeat at RAMS Park through substitute Deniz Gul's 77th-minute header.

And Garnacho failed to make the travelling party to Istanbul, despite Emery naming two back-up goalkeepers and opting to fill only 11 of the 12 available options on the bench.

The Argentine is on a season-long loan from Chelsea, with his deal including an obligation to buy if certain conditions were met, but he has made just seven appearances in all competitions, with none of those coming from the start.

Garnacho has also failed to make the previous two Premier League squads – both games Villa drew – and Emery seemingly confirmed the winger was not in his immediate plans.

"The players who were here are who I think are the best players to be here with us," said Emery.

Villa have lost successive games in major European competition for the first time since a run of three in April/May 2024 in the Conference League.

It is also the first time since November 2024 that they have failed to score in successive outings in major European competitions.

— Aston Villa (@AstonVilla) November 24, 2026

Indeed, Villa failed to record a shot on target in a game for the third time in all competitions this season; prior to this campaign, they had recorded at least one in all previous 196 games under Emery.

The Spaniard was frustrated, claiming the surface also hindered his team.

"Disappointed a little bit," Emery said. "After their goal, it was impossible to play.

"They wasted time. They added only five minutes. OK. Finish the match. We don't want to play more. I don't think the referee was fair there. It is like that.

"Two years ago, we lost to [Club] Brugge and Monaco away. I can compare this match like those matches.

"Why? Because their supporters are pushing so much. The pitch was not helping. The match was difficult because they pressed intense.

"We did a fantastic job in the first half. We stopped them from keeping the ball and going long. We avoided transitions. It was not enough because we lacked offensively."

Maximilian Beier equalised after the break and despite the hosts pushing constantly for a winner, it would not come.

Matt Verri was at the Emirates Stadium to rate the Arsenal players...

#1679. Arsenal can equal two all-time Champions League records in Borussia Dortmund battle

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 09:09

Arsenal will be bidding to equal two all-time Champions League records when they welcome Borussia Dortmund to the Emirates Stadium for Tuesday's league-phase encounter.

Mikel Arteta's men reunite with the German giants 12 years on from their last head-to-head in November 2014, when the Spaniard captained Arsenal to a 2-0 victory in North London.

The Gunners could end the evening top of the Champions League league phase table too, if they overcome Dortmund and Real Madrid - who are two points clear - either lose to PSV Eindhoven or draw and fall behind on goal difference; Paris Saint-Germain are not in action until Wednesday.

Arsenal have accrued 10 points from their opening four continental games this season, overcoming Lille, Slavia Prague and Napoli and only dropping points in an encapsulating 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich.

After also navigating the entire 2025-26 league phase unbeaten, Arsenal could firstly equal their own club record of 17 straight Champions League group stage/league phase games without suffering defeat.

Arteta's men have won 15 and drawn one of their 16 league-phase games since a 1-0 loss to Inter Milan in November 2024, and they have only ever gone 17 unbeaten at this stage between 2003 and 2006.

That record streak began with a 1-0 victory over Dynamo Kyiv in November 2003, and ended when Arsene Wenger's men suffered a 1-0 defeat to CSKA Moscow in 2006.

Additionally, Arsenal have won each of their last 12 Champions League group stage/league phase games at the Emirates and could equal the English football record for the longest victorious run on home soil.

The only Premier League team to win more successive UCL league phase/group stage games at home is Liverpool, who triumphed in 13 on the spin between 2020 and 2025.

Ever since their return to the Champions League in the 2023-24 season, Arsenal have been almost perfect at home in the group stage/league phase, and their 12-game winning run is a sight to behold.

Arteta's side kicked off their triumphant streak with a 4-0 rout of PSV Eindhoven in September 2023, before Sevilla and Lens were bested in the same year.

The 2024-25 group stage saw Paris Saint-Germain, Shakhtar Donetsk, Monaco and Dinamo Zagreb conquered in North London, while Olympiacos, Bayern Munich, Atletico Madrid and Kairat Almaty fell to Arsenal's Emirates might in 2025-26.

The Gunners' only home encounter in Europe so far this season ended in a 3-0 success over Lille, and they have scored a remarkable 36 goals while conceding just three during their 12-match sequence.

Thanks to Arsenal's prolonged absence from the Champions League between 2017 and 2023, it has been almost exactly 10 years since they last failed to win a group stage/league phase game at the Emirates; a 2-2 draw with Paris Saint-Germain on November 23, 2016.

#1678. Can Ethan Nwaneri play against Arsenal for loan club Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League tonight?

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal dropped points from a winning position for the second time in as many games following a 1-1 Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium.

Mikel Arteta’s men led at the interval after Viktor Gyokeres scored his first goal on home soil in 206 days with a wonderful 25-yard opener inside 10 minutes.

But just as they did in the Premier League at Newcastle on Saturday, Arsenal were unable to see out the victory, with Maximilian Beier netting for the visitors after half-time.

Jobe Bellingham had a goal ruled out for offside, while Gyokeres could perhaps count himself fortunate not to give away a penalty when a Dortmund corner struck him on the arm.

Gyokeres then wasted a golden opportunity to restore Arsenal’s advantage when he headed wide unmarked from six yards, while the ball cannoned off Serhou Guirassy to twice strike the Dortmund post in the closing stages. Declan Rice hit the woodwork again for Arsenal with five minutes left.

The draw leaves Arsenal fifth in the table, but they could be on the bubble of the top-eight places – which are assured of automatic qualification for the next phase – if results work against them on Wednesday.

Gyokeres was introduced only as a stoppage-time substitute in Arsenal’s 2-2 draw at St James’ Park despite the Gunners chasing the game for most of the second half.

Here, he began from the start and opened the scoring with his first meaningful contribution of the game.

Noni Madueke had time and space to bring down a crossfield ball before finding Gyokeres, who immediately tried his luck from range, and perhaps catching Gregor Kobel in the visiting goal by surprise.

But that was to take away nothing from the velocity and dip behind Gyokeres’ effort – the sort of strike which encouraged Arsenal to spend £68million last summer but has not always been repaid. It was Gyokeres’ first at the Emirates since May.

Rice fired over from range and then only a last-ditch tackle from Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck denied the England midfielder moments later. Arsenal led at the break, but they did in the North East before a second-half collapse saw them emerge with just a point, rather than three.

Why Arteta must erase Arsenal habit after Champions League frustration

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

Beier afforded Arsenal a warning almost immediately after the interval when he ghosted to the front post only to fail to get any sort of connection on Daniel Svensson’s low cross.

But Beier made no mistake in the 55th minute. Joane Gadou was the architect following a fine run from inside his own half. He looked up to find Beier, who took one touch past Gabriel before unleashing a low drive. Kepa Arrizabalaga, deputising for the injured David Raya, never got close to saving it.

Piero Hincapie’s header was saved by Kobel as Arsenal mustered a response. Bellingham thought he had put Dortmund ahead when he turned away Kepa’s bungled save but the assistant referee’s offside flag came to Arsenal’s rescue.

Then came the Arsenal onslaught. Madueke’s curling shot grazed the side-netting before Gyokeres sent a diving header wide from six yards to leave Arteta on his knees. Arsenal also struck a post on three occasions.

In all, the Gunners had 29 shots but only four of those were on target, and the need for a world-class finisher remains a top priority should Arsenal want to win the Champions League for the first time in their history. They will face Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid next.

#1676. Rabiot and Ruben’s rampant Rossoneri: All the key stats from AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone

AC Milan produced their best attacking display of the season on Sunday night as they put five goals past Frosinone at San Siro.

An own-goal from Gabriele Calvani early on set the tone, with Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netting in the rout. The ruthless counter-attacking display moves Milan back inside the top four, after wins from Como, Roma and Lazio earlier in the round.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The match stats make for interesting reading. Milan edged possession with 54%, generating 2.50 Expected Goals – so scoring double what they created – but also having five big chances which matches the number of goals scored.

Frosinone remarkably had more shots in total (15 to 12), but they were more wasteful with only three on target to the Rossoneri’s eight. The visitors also racked up nine corners, the most Milan have conceded all season.

📊 The stats from the win against Frosinone. pic.twitter.com/ERVTj98m9Y

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 22, 2026

Only Nereo Rocco’s (29) and Lajos Czeizler’s (31) Milan sides scored more goals than Ruben Amorim’s (28) in their first 12 matches in charge in Serie A.

Adrien Rabiot is the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal (including goals and assists) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004, and he became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A with more than 10 goals in his first 10 games in a single season.

With his sixth goal in his 10th Serie A appearance for Milan at 20 years and 31 days, Alphadjo Cisse became the second-youngest Rossoneri player to reach this milestone in his first 10 appearances in the three-points-for-a-win era, after Alexandre Pato , who achieved it at 18 years and 189 days.

No team has scored more goals than Milan in the first 15 minutes of play in the five major European leagues currently underway (7, like Barcelona and Chelsea).

Milan are now unbeaten in all seven meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W5 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

Milan have won five of their last six league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in a run of Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

#1675. ‘Incredible’ Arsenal dropped two points in Dortmund draw – Madueke

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Arsenal dropped two points in their 1-1 Champions League draw against Borussia Dortmund, so says Noni Madueke.

The Gunners were dominant in the first half at Emirates Stadium, where Viktor Gyokeres' stunner put them into a 10th-minute lead.

Yet Arsenal could not add to their lead, and Dortmund stepped up in the second half, equalising in the 55th minute through Maximilian Beier.

Jobe Bellingham saw a goal disallowed, but Arsenal came on strong late on, with Gyokeres squandering a golden chance, while the Gunners hit the post twice.

Arsenal's 30 shots are their most on record in a Champions League game (since 2003-04), and the Gunners' most in a game that they failed to win across all competitions since December 2023 v West Ham.

And while Madueke felt some of Arsenal's play was "incredible", he acknowledged Mikel Arteta's team are frustrated.

He told Amazon Prime: "I feel like the performance from us up until the last shot was incredible at times.

"Definitely feels like two points dropped. A bit of frustration; need to get all three points, I think."

Honours even in N5. https://t.co/quJELEQP8x

Gyokeres echoed Madueke's sentiment, though he is confident Arsenal will get better results if they keep on creating so many chances.

"We could have scored in the second half. We could have won the game in many different ways," he told Amazon Prime.

"We played well and created a lot of chances, we deserved to win the game but sometimes it is like that.

"The most important thing is that we create those chances and get shots on goal. For sure we will score goals."

Arsenal have failed to win a home game in the group stage of major European competition for the first time since November 2019 (2-1 defeat v Eintracht Frankfurt), ending a run of 18 successive victories – the longest such winning run by any side in major European competition history.

Arteta said: "The performance was superb and there is no question about that from the start to the end. We played against a really good side and the domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more.

"I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball."

The Gunners are, though, only the third English side in Champions League history to go 20 successive matches unbeaten (W14 D6), after Manchester City between 2022 and 2024 (26) and Manchester United between 2007 and 2009 (25).

Now, their focus will turn to a huge Premier League clash with Man City on Sunday.

"I think these are the best games. I'm really looking forward to it," Madueke added.

"Two draws on the bounce now and I just desperately want to win on the weekend and I know my team-mates feel the same.

"We are going to do everything we have to win the three points. We're champions, we're at home. We have a duty to perform well at the Emirates. There are things we need to improve but all in all we are going in the right direction."

But just as they did in the Premier League at Newcastle on Saturday, Arsenal were unable to see out the victory, with Maximilian Beier netting for the visitors after half-time.

Gyokeres then wasted a golden opportunity to restore Arsenal’s advantage when he headed wide unmarked from six yards, while the ball cannoned off Serhou Guirassy to twice strike the Dortmund post in the closing stages. Declan Rice hit the woodwork again for Arsenal with five minutes left.

The draw leaves Arsenal fifth in the table, but they could be on the bubble of the top-eight places – which are assured of automatic qualification for the next phase – if results work against them on Wednesday.

Gyokeres was introduced only as a stoppage-time substitute in Arsenal’s 2-2 draw at St James’ Park despite the Gunners chasing the game for most of the second half.

Here, he began from the start and opened the scoring with his first meaningful contribution of the game.

Noni Madueke had time and space to bring down a crossfield ball before finding Gyokeres, who immediately tried his luck from range, and perhaps catching Gregor Kobel in the visiting goal by surprise.

But that was to take away nothing from the velocity and dip behind Gyokeres’ effort – the sort of strike which encouraged Arsenal to spend £68million last summer but has not always been repaid. It was Gyokeres’ first at the Emirates since May.

Rice fired over from range and then only a last-ditch tackle from Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck denied the England midfielder moments later. Arsenal led at the break, but they did in the North East before a second-half collapse saw them emerge with just a point, rather than three.

Beier afforded Arsenal a warning almost immediately after the interval when he ghosted to the front post only to fail to get any sort of connection on Daniel Svensson’s low cross.

But Beier made no mistake in the 55th minute. Joane Gadou was the architect following a fine run from inside his own half. He looked up to find Beier, who took one touch past Gabriel before unleashing a low drive. Kepa Arrizabalaga, deputising for the injured David Raya, never got close to saving it.

Piero Hincapie’s header was saved by Kobel as Arsenal mustered a response. Bellingham thought he had put Dortmund ahead when he turned away Kepa’s bungled save but the assistant referee’s offside flag came to Arsenal’s rescue.

Then came the Arsenal onslaught. Madueke’s curling shot grazed the side-netting before Gyokeres sent a diving header wide from six yards to leave Arteta on his knees. Arsenal also struck a post on three occasions.

In all, the Gunners had 29 shots but only four of those were on target, and the need for a world-class finisher remains a top priority should Arsenal want to win the Champions League for the first time in their history. They will face Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid next.

#1673. Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

Despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Emery said: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

“It’s very important to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

Their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

Villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

Jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Villa defended resolutely as time began to tick away with Suzuki providing authority in goal. The first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Champions League also produced a number of routine saves in a nervy finish.

This was a promising night for a new Villa era.

Full-time scenes in Bruges as Aston Villa get their Champions League campaign off to a winning start! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nYwtiQ6Xs7

Villa are defending with six at the back as midfield and defence merge into one. There are seconds remaining as Suzuki punts the ball up field and there is the final whistle! Villa make a winning start to the 2026-27 Champions League.

Another cross from the right is met, this time, by Tresoldi, but his header has no bite and Suzuki gathers.

Torres heads another Siquet cross behind for a corner. Brugge load the box but none of their players are able to get a meaningful touch on the ball before Diakhon slips just as he looks to get a shot away from the left of the box.

Slightly less mature play from Gomes, though. He bundles Vermant over and earns a needless yellow card.

Really mature play by Hemmings. Looking to break away, he simply puts his body between man and ball, inviting the challenge and winning a foul.

Villa are working hard in their compact mid-block and Brugge are struggling to find a way through.

Leko sends on Vermant and Diakhon for Potts and Virgili.

Barkley is one lucky boy. Attempting to play out under pressure, the midfielder gives the ball straight to Virgili, who cannot sort out his feet before offloading to Tresoldi far too late. A big let-off for Villa.

Gomes goes close after driving through Brugge’s midfield. He really should, though, have played in a free McGinn at the back post. Moments later Bogarde fires another shot goalwards but Sommer gets to it.

Villa have wrestled control away from their opponents. McGinn’s teasing cross evades everyone and Alysson’s cross takes a deflection which goes behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Lee hauls down Hemmings which gives Villa the opportunity to slow the game down. McGinn flights a delivery in from the left but Brugge clear their lines.

The ball comes out to Alysson who jinks in from the right, tiptoeing through a crowd, desperate to get a shot away on his left foot, but Seys does well to track his man and smother the effort.

Vanakan and Velesen and replaced by Tsawa and Lemarechal.

Yet another dangerous Siquet cross rains in from the right and here it is taken off Tresoldi’s toes by the tip of Lindelof’s boot. The defender did brilliantly to clear his lines at full stretch.

Hemmings burst towards the by-line and his cross trickles across the face of goal. Alysson is waiting at the far post but Seys does well to shield the ball and win a free-kick.

Villa’s best chance at putting this game to bed will come on the counter. And here McGinn plays in Jackson whose one-vs-one effort is stopped by Sommer.

Virgili from the left, Siquet from the right. Threats are coming from both wings and Villa need to get their foot on the ball if they are to take the sting out of Brugge’s attack.

Instead they allow Vetlesen a yard of space and his long-range sighter stings the hands of Suzuki who turns behind for a corner.

Emery switches out Buendia, Kamara and Wan-Bissaka for Alysson, Barkley and Bogarde before the corner is taken, and Suzuki stops the eventual delivery on the line after the ball spun off the post!

Another Virgili cross threatens to carve Villa open but they just about clear their lines. Then it is Siquet who delivers, this time from the right, but his cross just evades Tresoldi and Mechele at the far post. The home fans are invested in this, they believe their side can grab an equaliser...

Villa have got their tails between their legs here. From a position of strength, they have allowed the momentum to swing in the hosts’ favour and it has been largely self-inflicted.

Maatsen has a chance to break free but cannot build a head of steam before he is stymied.

Club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3 (Tresoldi pen) Suzuki dives to his right early and Tresoldi slides the ball into the opposite side of the net. Just the one goal in it now!

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Brugge have averted their attention to their right hand side, Siquet and Forbs attacking in tandem. A dangerous cross from Forbs is met by Tresoldi but he cannot get the requisite contact on it. Seys collects the ball on the far side and fires a delivery into Wan-Bissaka and out for a corner. Replays show that it comes off the defenders hand ...and referee Scharer is sent to the screen. He wastes no time at the monitor and awards a spot kick!

Villa do appear pretty comfortable here, despite some frequent pressure from Club Brugge.

Pau Torres has been outstanding so far at the back for Unai Emery’s team.

This is also a night where Emery’s ‘new’ Villa are coming of age, with Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and Joao Gomes also impressive.

Virgili then darts in field from his starting perch on the left. Tresoldi backheels the ball back into his path but Virgili’s effort is snuffed out.

McGinn, sensing Virgili’s growing influence on the half, takes matters into his own hands and leaves one on the Spanish winger, Siquet’s free-kick from deep is aimed at Tresoldi but Suzuki is wise to it and sweeps up.

Brugge are just reminding Villa that they are still there. Virgili is at the heart of things again, combining with Vetlesen who works the ball out to Forbs whose cross is well held by Suzuki.

Villa then spring forward, Hemmings breaching the Brugge box, but Buendia’s eventual effort does not make it through a thicket of legs.

Brugge are building with a three-man backline, sending Siquet forward high and wide. They’ve had much of the ball in the opening stages of this half, which is probably part of Villa’s plan. Emery’s side have settled into an out-of-possession 4-4-2.

Vanakan is booked for simulation after going hitting the deck off a challenge from Gomes. There is a knowing smile on the Belgian midfielder’s face which suggests the referee’s convictions were correct.

We are back under way... Siquet replaces Sabbe at the interval.

Nicolas Jackson is off the mark for Aston Villa. He beat Yann Sommer to the ball, held off a defender and was left with the simplest of finishes to round off a fine first half for Villa. pic.twitter.com/gWx6kUTlOX

Unai Emery has the new kids on the block but this Aston Villa team are hangin’ tough.

This has been a pretty chaotic first-half on the return of the Champions League but Emery will be satisfied with what he has seen so far. It’s very much a case of step by step for his reshaped team, but they should see this game out now.

It’s been a shocking night for Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper Yann Sommer. He’s just had a serious rush of blood to the head and was punished by Nicolas Jackson, who had an easy task to score Villa’s third goal. Sommer has probably ended his team’s hopes of a result here.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 3 (Jackson) A shocker from Brugge, but in particular Sommer. Jackson races on to a nothing punt over the top by Torres, and the situation appears under control with two defenders in the striker’s orbit, but Sommer comes steaming out and Jackson nudges the ball past him before sliding it home into a vacant net.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

A sloppy Torres pass out from the back goes straight to Vetlesen who picks out Forbs first time. The winger unleashes an effort from range but Suzuki makes a smart stop.

There is a shout for a Villa handball as Virgili prods a cross on to Kamara’s body, but his arms are clearly by his side.

Villa are presented with a great opportunity to break but the pass in behind for Jackson to gallop on to does not have enough juice and the move breaks down. Jackson does have a sight at goal moments later, but he’s only able to poke the ball wide off a free-kick from the right.

A really sloppy piece bit of play from Vanakan who cedes possession to Jackson and he’s straight into Brugge’s backline. He releases the ball to McGinn but the midfielder’s looping cross is cleared. Brugge need to take better care with the detail on their passes.

Jackson escapes the clutches of his marker on the half-way line with a deft spin and he feeds McGinn whose shot is blocked. The ball is worked to Hemmings after Torres is afforded space once more and a block takes it behind for a corner. Villa go short but the routine comes to nothing.

Maatsen flashes a dangerous delivery across the face of goal but the ball bisects Jackson and Buendia precisely and Brugge are able to clear their lines.

Brugge have certainly not given up the ghost, still looking to work the ball out to Forbs and Virgili on the flanks. Sabbe overlaps down the right but his ball to Vetlesen is cut out and Villa attempt to spring a counter which is snuffed out by Mechele.

Villa midfielder Joao Gomes is having a productive evening as he aims to recover from that nightmare debut.

He was sent off after 40 minutes of his first Villa appearance in the excruciating 4-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion.

Unai Emery is expecting big things from the Brazilian midfielder, who departed relegated Wolves for £38m in July.

Wan-Bissaka drives down the right as Villa look for a third, but his cross is overhit and goes off on the far side. The right intent, though.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 2 (Buendia) Jackson holds up the ball expertly before slipping in Gomes. The midfielder bursts into the box, outwitting Vetlesen before cutting the ball back to an onrushing Buendia who clips the ball past Sommer with aplomb. A crazy couple of minutes!

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 1 (Vetlesen) Brugge are getting a lot of joy down the flanks. This time it is Vetlesen who finds space down the right and he spears a cross into the box. The ball is worked out to the left where the dangerous Virgili sends the ball back into the area and there Vetlesen is to sweep home. The stadium erupts as the Belgian champions restore parity.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

The Jan Breydelstadion had been very noisy but that goal has completely changed the atmosphere.

It is now nervy in the stadium and the Brugge fans are already starting to boo some of their players.

Villa’s first goal of the season and no surprise it comes from their talisman John McGinn.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

Close! Hemmings races on to a cutback but his effort trickles just wide of the post.

Goalkeeper Sommer is penalised for handling the ball outside of his box. He had gathered a corner and had stormed forward to set off an attack. He changes his mind mid-throw and attempts to re-catch the ball but ends up wandering outside of his allotted space. The resulting free-kick crashes straight into the wall.

Sommer with an accidental handball outside his area! 😳📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fBbqPEYyUJ

Club Brugge 0 Aston Villa 1 (McGinn) Brugge will be really disappointed with that. Torres is afforded the freedom of Flanders as he strides up from his own half to the edge of the hosts’ box. He offloads the ball to McGinn on the right of the area and the Scotsman steadies himself before curling the ball into the far post, beyond Sommer.

It is that duo again, Virgili and Seys. They have responded to Wan-Bissaka’s advanced position and are trying to pin him back. Virgili cuts in on to his right foot and forces a save from Suzuki to get the home fans going.

Aston Villa are still establishing their identity with a new team but it has already become clear how much they will rely on goalkeeper Zion Suzuki,

The £30m signing from Parma possesses a wide passing range and much of Villa’s build-up play starts with the Japan international.

He is Villa’s very own version of Manchester City’s former pass master Ederson.

Much has been made of Suzuki’s distribution and he has already teased a couple of lovely flighted balls up-field. Villa’s defenders are more than happy to lure Brugge’s first line of pressure forward but have not yet been able to find an incisive line-breaking pass.

Seyes and Virgili combine down the left in Brugge’s best attack so far, but Torres is able to head behind for a corner, which is not up to much.

Wan-Bissaka has taken up a very aggressive position down Villa’s right and he earns a free-kick in a promising position. McGinn spins in a delivery which is only partially cleared but Maatsen’s effort from the edge of the box is smothered.

Villa get their foot on the ball from the get-go, circulating the ball around the back, before Suzuki launches a long ball up to Wan-Bissaka. The ball is worked to McGinn who feeds Buendia on the edge of the box but his effort flies just wide.

There is a minute’s silence for those affected by the floods in Nepal which is impeccably observed.

The players then retreat to their halves and Jackson gets us going!

Brugge and Villa emerge from the tunnel to the Champions League anthem... Here is this season’s introductory VT to whet the appetite.

The Champions League is back. #UCL pic.twitter.com/bsFGV69KMP

"This is a good test and challenge for us today." 💪Aston Villa boss Unai Emery looks ahead to their Champions League clash with Club Brugge.🎙️ @LiamMacdevitt | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h4NF1jmiW6

As the rain lashes down in Bruges, you get the sense that Villa will have to dig deep to get a result and breathe life into their season. Both teams thrive on attacking transitions and the surface-level moisture will encourage breakaway moves.

Opta’s supercomputer has worked its magic again this season and placed Villa as the 10th favourites to lift the Champions League trophy. Back-to-back winners Paris St-Germain are only fifth. Here are the leading contenders before a ball has been kicked.

Agree? Leave your thoughts in the comments section beneath this live blog...

Aston Villa 2.0 is clearly a work in progress after so many high-profile exits and 10 new signings.

Unai Emery has warned that it will take time for his new team to click, but this is an opportunity to spark the season into life.

Behind the scenes, Villa are feeling very comfortable about so much upheaval and it is the presence of Emery in the technical area which provides them with so much optimism.

For a deeper dive into why patience will be needed, read more here.

Brugge have conceded just two goals in five league games this season, but their Pro League opponents have threatened against the Belgian champions’ right side, especially in attacking transitions. Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

Here are a couple of examples of Brugge’s vulnerability down their right:

Don-Angelo Konadu, Lommel’s centre-forward, drifts out to the left and takes on Lee Han-beom whose centre-back partner Brandon Mechele has committed too far forward. As such, the space between Lee and covering left-back Joaquin Seys is too big and Freddie Potts attempts to recover from midfield. Konadu earns himself a yard with a feint inside and his shot is well-saved by Yann Sommer.

In Brugge’s 2-1 defeat by Gent a week earlier, Leonardo Lopes punches in a pass into the left half-space for Monodu Sonko to latch on to and from there the inside forward draws a save from Sommer. Josué Vergara’s follow-up strikes the crossbar.

The Spaniard added a fifth Europa League title to his CV last season while also guiding Villa to a strong fourth-place finish in the Premier League. Emery was today announced as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

Christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

While Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

He was signed from West Ham last month for a significant fee and lifted the Europa Conference League trophy when David Moyes was in charge.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.

Club Brugge Sommer; Sabbe, Lee, Mechele, Seys; Potts, Vanaken; Forbs, Vetlesen, Virgili; Tresoldi

Substitutes Audoor, Coulibaly, Diakhon, Jackers, Lemarechal, Mike, Siquet, Spileers, Tsawa, Vanden Driessche, Vasovic, Vermant

Aston Villa Suzuki; Wan-Bissaka, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; McGinn, Buendia, Hemmings; Jackson

Substitutes Abraham, Barkley, Bizot, Bogarde, Garnacho, Mbaye, Mings, Ruggeri, Wright, Alysson

One player who will have many memories of this stadium is Villa centre-back Tyrone Mings.

Who can forget that bewildering moment in November 2024 when Mings picked up the ball inside the penalty area?

Club Brugge are awarded a penalty after Tyrone Mings picks the ball up inside his own area 😳📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/wpAqjMW8pn

Everybody loves a redemption story and on his return a few months later he produced a brilliant individual performance which included an incredible goal-line clearance to save his team.

Mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle issue so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He said: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

“We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [big] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

“We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a new test.”

The experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

Our ground crew for tonight. 👥📃 pic.twitter.com/UB7FUi9ZDH

Emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

How we start this evening to take on Club Brugge in the #UCL 👊 pic.twitter.com/d7ftzgnoIi

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a new-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of big-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s new-look crew.

Morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his new recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

#1672. Man United transfer news: Red Devils want three January signings, seven targets identified

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 09:31

Struggling on the pitch, Manchester United are already preparing for the January transfer window with three positions targeted and seven options identified.

19th in the Premier League, Manchester United are going through a sporting crisis. Mauricio Pochettino has just arrived to replace Michael Carrick. The Argentinian boss will try to halt the negative spiral, while the hierarchy is already preparing its next January transfer window.

The Manchester club intend to use January to strengthen their squad. According to TeamTalk, the club's decision-makers have identified three priority positions: centre-back, left-back and centre-forward. Signing a centre-back is Manchester United's main priority.

The club already have three profiles in mind: Calvin Bassey (Fulham), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton) and Nathan Collins (Brentford).

The club's executives have reportedly already made enquiries about all three players. A permanent transfer would, however, be needed to convince any of these clubs, with a loan not being considered in these cases.

A large part of the winter budget should therefore be devoted to this signing. Manchester United's January budget is reportedly £50m, according to the Daily Mail. That is a rather small amount to strengthen in three positions and cover for the shortcomings of a squad in the midst of doubt.

In attack, Manchester United want to sign a centre-forward capable of providing more competition. Two options stand out: Folarin Balogun (Monaco) and Ivan Toney (Al-Ahli). A loan with an option to buy is reportedly being considered for both forwards, while Joshua Zirkzee could leave in January.

The club want to provide an additional solution on the left flank, where Luke Shaw lacks competition and availability.

Two players are particularly liked: Alejandro Balde (Barcelona) and Rayan Ait-Nouri (Manchester City). Talks have reportedly already taken place with both clubs.

Both full-backs could leave in January as they play little at their respective clubs. Manchester United would favour a loan for one of these deals. The club have therefore already drawn up their roadmap, but the sporting situation and the meagre budget will not make it easy for them to strengthen.

#1671. Leny Yoro: Manchester United make Pro Ref decision amid Mauricio Pochettino red card rage

Manchester United are furious at referees’ chief Howard Webb’s support for the decision to send off Leny Yoro at Liverpool, despite the defender having his one-match suspension removed.

The French centre-back was dismissed after only eight minutes of United’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield on Sunday for fouling Reds striker Alexander Isak as he advanced towards goal, with referee Sam Barrott deciding Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

United successfully appealed for wrongful dismissal and the suspension has now been removed, the Football Association has confirmed, meaning Yoro is free to play in the Premier League match against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Liverpool scored their opening goal directly from the free-kick awarded for Yoro’s challenge.

One question raised was whether Isak had the ball sufficiently under control for this to count as denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity. The Swede’s touch took the ball into the arms of United goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Pro Ref’s chief refereeing officer Webb backed the decision to dismiss the 21-year-old, saying it was “certainly not clearly wrong”.

However, United boss Mauricio Pochettino vehemently disagreed and hit out at the lack of VAR intervention.

It is understood that the club are unhappy with Webb’s comments and plan to make their feelings known to Pro Ref.

Speaking at a press conference ahead of his team’s Champions League match against Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday, the Argentinian said: “Very disappointed. My question always was the same, we can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotion of the game, sometimes the view or the position can affect that. But if we have VAR, what were they doing?

“Now, are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play with similar tools – 11 v 11?

“We have an unbelievable car, but we need to have the level to drive, we need to drive in the best way. We love the technology, yes, and we accept the technology is there, but what are they doing? But it’s not only this mistake, it affects everything.

“No-one is talking about the [Dominik Szoboszlai’s] goal wasn’t legal, they should have disallowed the goal because [Bradley] Barcola was touching our wall. Maybe in the last two years the rules have changed while I was in America. Why didn’t they check it? It must be disallowed.”

Man Utd blow as Pochettino drops hint in Champions League squad

Man Utd star ‘opens door’ to January transfer after Pochettino arrival

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

Webb discussed the sending-off with former Liverpool and United striker Michael Owen in the latest edition of Match Officials: Mic’d Up, which aired on Tuesday evening but was recorded before the FA confirmed Yoro’s suspension had been removed.

“The reason we’re talking about it is the fourth consideration [in DOGSO decisions], that’s control or likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball,” Webb said.

“Isak’s got control of the ball, he’s got possession, he’s got the touch, he knocks it past Yoro. He’s moving at pace at that moment and a crowd comes in and knocks him down.

“There’s a question mark I guess around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.

“The VAR checks to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn’t.

“I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it’s a little bit debatable. (It’s) certainly not clearly wrong.”

VAR John Brooks was of the same opinion as he said in the audio between him and referee Barrott: “Let’s roll it through firstly to see whether the attacker is going to get on the end of the ball.

“Just roll through real speed. So, at full speed, Isak maintains his momentum and likely gets on the end of it.

“OK, certainly not clearly wrong that he doesn’t. So I think the DOGSO confirmed.”

#1670. Why Mikel Arteta must eradicate familiar Arsenal habit after Champions League frustration

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Here was Arsenal’s very own Groundhog Day.

Mikel Arteta would have feared what was coming as the misses piled up and his team found increasingly remarkable ways to not score.

Gyokeres nets stunner as Arsenal held by Dortmund in thriller

Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund LIVE: Latest score and updates Champions League

Man Utd make Pro Ref decision amid Pochettino red card rage

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

It was rinse and repeat from an Arsenal perspective. Completely dominate the opening 45 minutes with some sublime football. Take the lead but then fail to kick on. Drop the intensity in the second half and regret those missed opportunities.

That happened against Slavia Prague, when the Gunners just about held on in the second half to win. It happened on Saturday, when they had to come from behind just to draw a match they should have been three or four goals up in.

And it happened here, in perhaps the most ridiculous way yet. With some better decision-making in the final third, the Premier League champions might have put six past Dortmund.

Instead, from their 30 shots, Arsenal managed just four shots on target and one goal. The visitors rode their luck but they stayed within touch and when their moment came, Maximilian Beier took it with the kind of ruthlessness Arteta can only dream of.

It is unrealistic to expect the north Londoners to dominate a match for the full 90 minutes, even more so against Dortmund than the likes of Slavia Prague and Newcastle.

The problem is Arsenal’s lack of efficiency when they are on top means they cannot afford even the slightest drop in standards or intensity.

Score the two or three goals that the dominance deserves in the first half and a dip after the break will not be so decisive. As it is, with Arsenal leaving the margins so thin, one moment is all it takes for the hard work to be undone.

At St James’ Park, that moment was Odegaard mis-kicking a clearance. Here, it was Joane Gadou charging away from Christos Tzolis and nobody in the home midfield coming across to cover.

The match should have been done by then. Again, Arsenal were sensational in the first 45 minutes.

Noni Madueke, a constant threat, could not sort his feet out quickly enough when a rebound fell to him. The winger was then completely open, screaming for the ball shortly after when Declan Rice instead went by himself and had his shot deflected wide.

Counters were wasted. Viktor Gyokeres, who opened the scoring with a superb strike from distance, suddenly could not hit the target. When Arsenal went in only 1-0 up, what followed next was as predictable as it was galling for the Gunners.

The level dropped just slightly and the Bundesliga leaders came back into the game, equalising ten minutes after the restart.

Even then, though, Arsenal should have been able to recover. Unlike against Slavia Prague or Newcastle, Arsenal did not fall away for an extended period. This match was there for them to win and the chances came thick and fast.

Gyokeres headed wide from a few yards out. The Arsenal fans spent almost the entire final half an hour screaming at the players to shoot as extra touches were taken around the area.

When Serhou Guirassy then bounced the ball off his body onto his own post not once but twice, Arteta collapsed to the ground in disbelief.

The winner would not come. A top-two finish, which was so important in last season’s run to the final, has now become much harder.

But that is what this side keep doing. They seem determined to make things hard for himself. Another match that should have been won inside an hour turned into a 90-minute slugfest.

With Arsenal hoping this is another long season domestically and in Europe, it is a habit they must shake fast.

#1669. ‘Mismatch’: Jobe Bellingham reveals Arsenal weakness that Borussia Dortmund exploited

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Jobe Bellingham has revealed an Arsenal weakness that he and Borussia Dortmund looked to exploit in their Champions League encounter.

The Bundesliga leaders left the Emirates Stadium with a share of the spoils after Maximilian Beier’s equaliser cancelled out Viktor Gyokeres’ stunning opener in the first half.

The Gunners had plenty of chances to kill the game off and secure all three points, but Declan Rice hit the post, Noni Madueke went close a number of times and Gyokeres missed a gilt-edged opportunity from close range as they were forced to settle for a stalemate.

Post-match, Bellingham, fresh off his maiden senior England call-up, said that there had been a “mismatch” that he was instructed to take advantage of in midfield.

“One of the coaches pointed out to me that I was against Myles [Lewis-Skelly],” he explained on Amazon Prime Video.

“For the long ball - I don’t want to say a mismatch - but I’m obviously bigger.

“You would expect that if I was against Gabriel or Ezri [Konsa] it would be a bit more difficult to win the long balls. I thought that there was a bit of an advantage there in terms of height. I managed to win a few flick-ons and get us up the pitch.

“We varied it well, we played short, and we retained possession and defended a lot better in transitions.”

Jobe, the younger brother of Real Madrid star Jude, was unfortunate not to hit the winner as he followed in Julian Ryerson’s saved shot, which Kepa Arrizabalaga spilled.

The midfielder was alive to tuck away the rebound, only to be flagged for offside to deny him a first goal of the season.

“Gutted,” the 21-year-old continued, “A bit unlucky at the minute. It would have been nice if it was today, back in England.”
